entries.summary: How a bishop is elected by the cathedral canons, what candidate qualifications mean in game terms (Latin literacy and usually a positive Church reputation), and the grounds on which an election can be challenged by petition.
quotes: The bishop is elected by a simple majority, in a secret ballot, of the cathedral canons.

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Proctors
entries.summary: Proctors represent bishops, nobles or religious houses at the papal curia, presenting and appealing petitions, and are bound by four rules on tenure, concubinage, number per client and substitutes.
quotes: There are four rules for proctors:

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Ordination
entries.summary: Ordination is a seasonal activity ending in an oral examination: the Examination Total is compared with an Ease Factor set by the grade sought, with Reputation consequences for a very good or marginal result, a Faith Point on success, and appeal or petition when the exam is failed or botched.
quotes: Ordination Examination Total: Intelligence + (Church Lore or Civil and Canon Law) + stress die
If the character's Ordination Exam Total is more than double the required Ease Factor
misses the required Ease Factor by less than 6

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Rapid Ordinations
entries.summary: A character ordained through several grades at once, for example when elected bishop, still gains only a single Faith Point from ordination.

entries.title: Canon Courts
entries.summary: Explains who judges in the Church's courts, how clergy are shielded from secular justice, what falls under canon jurisdiction, how summons and judgments work, and how compurgation can acquit a defendant on character witnesses.
quotes: A person cannot be forced, except by papal decree, to attend a canon court further than two days travel from his diocese.

entries.title: Punishment
entries.summary: Lists the Church's punishments: excommunication, irregularity (which stops a cleric using Faith Points), monition, public penance, imprisonment in a religious house, fines and suspension of a benefice; canon courts may not impose death or physical punishment.
quotes: An irregular clergyman cannot make use of Faith Points.
An excommunicate character is cursed and receives no benefit from any of the Sacraments except penance

entries.title: Shedding of Blood
entries.summary: Lists what clerics are forbidden to do with regard to bloodshed, including sentencing, attending punishments, commanding fighting men and ordeals, and (for major orders) practising chirurgy.
quotes: Clerics are forbidden to shed blood.
In addition, clerics in major orders may not practice chirurgy.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.78 Ordeals

entries.title: Sanctuary
entries.summary: A church, churchyard and cemetery give fugitives a limited period of sanctuary during which blood may not be spilled.
quotes: Sanctuary is granted for up to 40 days

entries.title: Simony
entries.summary: Buying or selling sacred things is a canon crime; the buyer loses what was gained and the seller is fined and may be excommunicated for repeat offences.
quotes: The seller is fined twice the value of the transaction

entries.title: Tithes
entries.summary: Everyone owes the Church a tenth of income, and canon courts prosecute under-payment, a risk for Hermetic covenants that evade the tithe.
quotes: In 1220, everyone tithes a tenth of their income to the Church.

entries.title: Sorcery and Witchcraft
entries.summary: Minor sorcery is rarely heard in canon courts and usually earns a public penance, while serious sorcery is prosecuted by secular courts with death as a possible punishment.
quotes: A typical penance involves wearing a white sheet before the congregation

entries.title: The Benefice
entries.summary: Explains the benefice as the income attached to a parish, who may assign it, the legitimate reasons for a priest to be absent (study, service elsewhere, pluralism), and how licenses of absence and benefice exchanges are handled.

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: The Petition Total
entries.summary: The core procedure for getting the Church to act: a Petition Total, built from Communication or Presence plus Church Lore plus modifiers and with no die roll, is compared with an Ease Factor set by the request, with a list of example Ease Factors and rules for who can grant what, written versus audience petitions, and scribes.
quotes: Petition Church: Petition Total vs Petition Ease Factor
Written Petition Total: Com + Church Lore + Modifiers
Audience Petition Total: Pre + Church Lore + Modifiers

related.text: The Church Ch.2 Furthering the cultus

entries.title: Modifiers to the Petition Total
entries.summary: Lists the bonuses and penalties that supporters, donations, arguments based on Abilities, visions, miracles and reputation add to a Petition Total, how an argument is rolled, and which bonuses do not stack.
quotes: Argument Success: Int + Ability Score + stress die vs Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: Henri of Toulouse's Petition
entries.summary: A worked example of building a Petition Total for founding a monastery from a scribe's total plus several supporting modifiers.

entries.title: The Petition of the Parish of Long Melford
entries.summary: A second worked example of a Petition Total, for moving a parish's feast days.

entries.title: Acting Without Authority
entries.summary: Sets the highest Ease Factor of petition that a bishop or a priest may grant on his own authority, and notes that such decisions can still be questioned later and that characters may act beyond their authority at some risk.
quotes: A bishop (or equivalently ranked character) may grant any petition or take any action with an Ease Factor of up to 15 without consulting his peers or superiors.

entries.title: Appealing a Petition
entries.summary: An appeal is itself a petition whose Ease Factor to overturn is based on the original Petition Total, with a compromise offered if it falls only slightly short, and a penalty for appealing after the original season.
quotes: Ease Factor to Overturn a Petition: Original Petition Total + 3
Ease Factor to Open Negotiations for Compromise: Original Petition Total – 3
If an appeal is not made in the same season as the original petition, then the appeal has a –3 penalty to its Petition Total.

entries.title: Creating Game Statistics for a Church
entries.summary: Introduces describing a church with Build Points, Hooks and Boons in the same way a covenant is described, to show how the Church affects the saga.

entries.title: Basic Church Features
entries.summary: Explains how a church is built from Build Points, Hooks and Boons (major and minor), and gives the base Divine aura and Build Points for each kind of church from cathedral to chapel.
quotes: You may usually choose up to 10 points of Hooks for the church.
A parish church has a base Divine Aura of 4, and 250 build points.

entries.title: Church resources (Build Points)
entries.summary: Build Point costs for a church's resources: books, enchanted items, relics priced by Faith Score and powers, specialists and vis, mostly at the same cost as for a covenant.
quotes: Enchanted Item Cost: 1 Build Point per Level of Effect
Relic Cost: Cost for Faith Score + 5 Build Points per Power

entries.title: Hooks and Boons
entries.summary: Notes that most covenant Hooks and Boons from the core rules and Covenants also suit churches, with a few new church-specific ones added.
quotes: are suitable for a church, although some may require interpretation by the troupe

entries.title: Care of Souls
entries.summary: A priest spends a season preaching to his congregation on a virtue theme, giving willing parishioners a bonus to matching activities for the next year and the priest experience in Leadership, Area Lore or Church Lore; it can be replaced by the aura-tempering rules.
quotes: Care of souls has a Source Quality of 2 for the priest, in Leadership, Area Lore, or Church Lore.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.38 Tempering an Aura

entries.title: Visitations
entries.requires: Bishop, archdeacon or rural dean making visitations
entries.summary: Describes the yearly visitation of parishes by bishops and their deputies, its cost to the parish, retinue size limits by rank, and the experience a season of visitation earns the visitor and retinue.
quotes: A season spent on visitation is worth 2 exposure experience points in Church Lore, Civil and Canon Law, Area Lore, or Ride for the visitor and his retinue.

entries.title: Becoming a Monk or Nun
entries.summary: The procedure for entering a religious house: harsh testing on arrival, a probationary year as a novice, the three solemn vows, and rules on oblates and the admission of girls to nunneries.
quotes: The three chief vows that are sworn as solemn oaths are for chastity, poverty, and obedience.

entries.title: The Opus Dei, Divine Office
entries.summary: A timetable of the canonical hours, meals and chapter meetings in a monastery, giving the storyguide a guide to where monks are and what they are doing at any hour.
quotes: Roused from sleep by the sacristan with a bell, the monks attend the first service of the day.

entries.title: The Religious in Your Saga
entries.summary: Advice on playing a monk or nun in a saga: limited free seasons outside the house, how religious roles bring them into the wider world, and the economic importance of monasteries and their hospitality to travellers.
quotes: even the most trusted monk may seem unlikely to have more than one free season outside the monastery each year

entries.title: Monastic Roles and Positions
entries.requires: Playing a monk or nun with an office in a religious house
entries.summary: Describes the offices of a religious house (abbot or abbess, prior, terrar, cellarer, bursar, infirmarian, sacrist, hostillar, chancellor and others) with the Abilities, Social Status Virtue and reputation suited to each, useful for building monastic characters and contacts.
quotes: She has a reputation of level 4, either good or bad, in both the local community and the Church.

entries.title: Female Religious in the Covenant
entries.summary: When a female religious character may live at a covenant: beguines, penitents and anchoresses need the bishop's permission, a nun needs a harder petition, episcopal visits must be managed, and vows and Flaws should reflect the character's way of life.
quotes: a Petition Ease Factor of 9 is appropriate
the Petition Ease Factor is 12

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church
The Lion and the Lily p.106 Cunfin

entries.title: Options for Absent Players
entries.summary: Suggests using an enclosed religious or anchoress character for a player who cannot attend sessions, with ways of passing letters between the cell and the covenant.

entries.title: Characters in a Nunnery
entries.requires: Playing a nun or other woman of a nunnery
entries.summary: Advice on building nun characters: which Flaws, Virtues and Abilities fit, plus background types (the Scholar, the Refugee, the Prisoner, the Revolutionary) and which Virtues and Flaws explain why a woman ends up in a nunnery.
quotes: Most nuns come from a noble family, so Privileged Upbringing is a common Virtue.
Artes Liberales, Latin, and Church Lore are the Abilities expected of all nun characters, even if only at a low level

related.text: Chapter 4: The Rule and Religious Life

entries.title: The Anchoress' Rule (Ancrene Riwle)
entries.requires: Playing an anchoress or her servant
entries.summary: The rule governing an anchoress and her servants, covering speech, food, fasting, visitors, possessions and dress, which a player can adopt in part to make a character distinctively religious. Ends with ways a magical anchoress might slip out of her cell.
quotes: The primary requirements of obedience, chastity, and permanence of abode remain.

entries.title: Priests' Wives and Mistresses
entries.requires: Playing a priest's wife or companion
entries.summary: Character-option advice for a woman living with a priest: the troupe decides whether the union counts as a valid marriage and whether it is a Dark Secret, and suggests roles in the parish such as a sacristan's wife.
quotes: Troupes with a female player character who lives with a priest should decide whether the priest and his wife consider themselves to be living under valid vows of marriage, or whether they believe themselves to be in a sinful relationship.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.81-82

entries.title: Templar Papal Privileges
entries.summary: List of the legal and religious privileges granted to the Templars by papal bulls, such as keeping booty, freedom from tithes and oaths to outsiders, and their own clergy; useful for adjudicating how Templars interact with Church and lay authority.
quotes: The order may keep the booty it captures from Muslims.
They need not pay tithes on the produce of their own lands.

entries.title: Running a Templar Chapter Meeting
entries.summary: Storyguide options for staging a Templar chapter meeting (mundane, mystic or dark), with a pointer to the covenant rules for designing a priory or chapterhouse.
quotes: There are broadly three options, and elements from each can be combined.

entries.title: The Templar Grand Master
entries.summary: Powers and duties of the Templar grand master, including his spiritual authority over the order equal to that of a priest.
quotes: He may exercise Holy Influence over the order as if he were a priest.

entries.title: The Grand Master's Commanding Aura
entries.requires: Holding the office of Templar grand master
entries.summary: The office of Templar grand master bestows the Commanding Aura Virtue on its holder, treated as spiritually equal to an archbishop.
quotes: The grand master, as a position appointed by God, is the spiritual equivalent to an Archbishop, with a Magic Resistance of 10.

entries.title: The Grand Master's Seal
entries.requires: Holding the office of Templar grand master
entries.summary: The grand master's seal is a Divine relic with its own Faith Score and Divine Might, which also adds extra Magic Resistance against effects tied to one particular sin.
quotes: The seal has a Faith Score of 1, granting it a Divine Might of 10.

entries.title: Templar Brother-Knights
entries.requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-knight
entries.summary: Entry requirements, expected prior combat experience, group training and restrictions on possessions for Templar brother-knights, who are the core rank of the order.
quotes: By 1220, the Templars require a brother-knight to be of noble birth, the son of a secular knight, or the son of the daughter of a knight to be admitted to this rank.

entries.title: Templar Brother-Sergeants
entries.requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-sergeant
entries.summary: The commoner rank of the Templars, serving as foot soldiers and as administrators, artisans and craftsmen under the same rule as the brother-knights.
quotes: Brother-sergeants are from common backgrounds and social statuses, and are recruited from a wider area.

entries.title: Templar Brother-Priests
entries.requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-priest
entries.summary: How priests join the Templars and the sacramental authority they hold within the order, which exceeds that of local clergy.
quotes: They can give services, celebrate Mass, hear confessions, give absolution for most offenses (except grievous sins such as murder, simony, or heresy) and bury the dead.

entries.title: Templar Confreres and Consoeurs
entries.requires: Associate membership in the Knights Templar
entries.summary: Lay associate members of the Templars, who take vows without full profession and may keep their own homes, including temporary-vow pilgrims and wives of Templars.
quotes: Confreres and consoeurs cannot vote in chapter meetings but otherwise interact daily with full members

entries.title: Templar Chaplains and Petitioning
entries.summary: Templar clergy petition their own commanders, the grand master or the pope rather than bishops, and may act on their own authority up to a set Ease Factor for matters within the order.
quotes: Brother-priests may, without reference to any outside authority, perform any action with an Ease Factor of 18 or less

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Petitioning the Church

entries.title: Trained Group Combat (Templars)
entries.summary: Templars who train together for a season count as a trained group in combat; without that season together they cannot form one.
quotes: who train together for a season are considered a trained group for the purpose of combat

entries.title: Templars Calling on God's Aid
entries.summary: Templars routinely petition God's aid before battle, led by a brother-priest or, lacking one, the commanding Templar, using the Divine rules for calling on God's aid.
quotes: The Templar commander (or ranking Templar) may also call on God's aid if there is no brother-priest.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.41-42

entries.title: Templar Military Tactics
entries.summary: How Templars fight: the cavalry charge as the centerpiece, mercenary foot and archers, siege warfare, and the black and white banner that forbids retreat while raised and serves as the rallying point.
quotes: While the banner is raised, no Templar is permitted to retreat.

entries.title: Joining the Templars: The Membership Ritual
entries.summary: Step-by-step account of the traditional ceremony in which an applicant is questioned, tested with a menial task if a commoner, swears his vows and is invested with the mantle.
quotes: Then he then swears the vows of obedience, chastity, and poverty, and promises to conquer and defend Jerusalem.

entries.title: Joining the Templars as a Child
entries.summary: Children may enter the Templars as novices once old enough to bear arms, with each local commander judging fitness; orphans are usually directed elsewhere.
quotes: Ages of admission of children range from 11 to 14.

entries.title: The Templar Rule and Penances
entries.summary: Outline of the Templar Rule and its penalties, from losing the mantle for a year and a day to expulsion, with a list of the offenses that earn them.
quotes: There are seven major sections to the rule
Major punishments include the stripping of a Templar's mantle for a year and a day

entries.title: Playing a Templar Character
entries.summary: Three ways to make a Templar playable despite the strictness of the rule: loose discipline (with a Story Flaw if the rule is to matter), outside responsibilities, or a lone Templar at a remote outpost.
quotes: Templar characters should take an appropriate Story Flaw if they want to play through stories involving the rule and Templar restrictions.

entries.title: Templar Banking, Letters of Credit and Insurance
entries.summary: How the Templars handle deposits, letters of credit that can be redeemed at a distant priory, administration of pilgrims' assets, and a form of physical and spiritual insurance.
quotes: In exchange, they receive a letter from that priory stating the value of the deposit.

entries.title: Templars and the Wealthy Virtue
entries.summary: Templars may take the Wealthy Virtue or Poor Flaw, but these represent responsibilities, authority and free time within a regimented day instead of personal money.
quotes: Templar characters can take the Wealthy Major Virtue, and also the Poor Major Flaw.

entries.title: Creating Templar Characters
entries.requires: Templar membership (Brother-Knight, Brother-Priest, Brother-Sergeant or other Templar Virtue)
entries.summary: Explains how Templar characters are built, with Templar-specific Social Status Virtues that set which Ability groups may be taken at creation, who the character answers to, and starting Reputation. Includes the Templar Prestige and associate/servant options.
quotes: You may take Academic and Martial Abilities during character generation.
He starts with a Reputation of level 4 within the Templars.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.92

entries.title: Templar Equipment
entries.summary: Lists the standard issue arms, armor, clothing, horses and squires for Templar brother-knights and brother-sergeants, and how squires differ from chivalric squires.
quotes: Each brother-knight is issued with three horses and a squire

entries.title: Templar Ciphers
entries.summary: Rules for sending Templar encrypted messages and for breaking the cipher, either without the key by an outsider or by a Templar with high Organization Lore.
quotes: the player must succeed in an Intelligence + Artes Liberales (Arithmetic) roll against an Ease Factor of 21.
with an Intelligence + Organization Lore: Knights Templar roll against an Ease Factor of 12.

entries.title: Preaching
entries.summary: Rules guidance for popular preaching: preachers are handled as performers with the Profession: Preacher Ability and Reputation, may change listeners' Personality Traits or teach Lores, and can be a study source for listeners. Lay preachers and the unordained risk trouble if they stray into doctrine.
quotes: Reputation is everything, and preachers are perhaps best treated as performers using the Art & Academe rules
If a character dedicates a season of free time to following a preacher, the study source is equal to the Aesthetic Quality of the preacher's performance in the relevant Ability.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Care of Souls

entries.title: Joining the Franciscans
entries.requires: Franciscan friar or Poor Sister character
entries.summary: Explains how to build male and female Franciscan characters: the Mendicant Friar Virtue for men, and the Religious Social Status plus suitable Virtues and Flaws for women. Notes that the usual Monastic Vows requirement can be swapped for alternatives.
quotes: While the Virtue Mendicant Friar covers male Franciscan characters, it is not appropriate for female Franciscan characters.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: The Dominicans (character guidance)
entries.summary: Describes the Order of Preachers and advises that a Dominican character takes the Educated Virtue and, if male without a university degree, is usually sent to study theology and ordained.
quotes: A character wishing to be a member of the Order of Preachers will have the Educated Virtue

entries.title: Gaining information from locals
entries.summary: Getting locals to talk uses a Communication + Folk Ken roll, with the Ease Factor raised by the local's Suspicious Personality Trait.
quotes: An average Communication + Folk Ken roll is usually sufficient to get an individual to talk, but increase the Ease Factor by the local's Suspicious Personality Trait.

entries.title: Criminals
entries.summary: Abstract rules for nobles hiring criminals: Intrigue is used to hire them, their results can be resolved without playing a scene, and typical prices are given for assassination, beatings, bribes, kidnapping, sabotage, spying and treachery. A table gives the added difficulty for different kinds of sabotage.
quotes: the hiring character rolls Communication + Intrigue and uses the result in place of the proxy's roll, to determine the degree of success
Sabotage requires a Dexterity + Stealth + stress roll that exceeds the Perception + Awareness + stress roll of the most skilled sentry guarding the facility that the agent seeks to harm.

entries.title: Intrigue and the Art of Indirect Action
entries.summary: Graded Ease Factors for an Intelligence + Intrigue roll that uncover a noble's enmities, vices and secrets, or let the intriguer spread rumors or forged evidence to damage the target's Reputation. Time and cost scale with the Ease Factor, and targets or their friends may trace the culprit.
quotes: For Ease factors higher than 6, this takes (3 x Ease) days and costs at least (Ease / 3) pounds.
The following Ease Factors, for an Intelligence + Intrigue roll, demonstrate what a character might learn about potential allies, or the harm they may cause by spreading gossip.

versions.title: Intrigue and the Art of Indirect Action
versions.summary: Sidebar with an Intelligence + Intrigue roll table giving Ease Factors for learning about a noble target's enmities, vices and Flaws or for spreading and forging damaging information, plus the days and pounds each attempt costs.
quotes: For Ease Factors higher than 6, this takes (3 x Ease Factor) days and costs at least (Ease Factor / 3) pounds.

entries.title: Double Agents and Hostile Takeovers
entries.summary: Extends the Appendix agent rules: recruiting a rival's agent as a double or triple agent, and taking over a whole agency by impersonating its principal to use the Bond Strength he has built.
quotes: as soon as the Resistance of the agent reaches zero, he becomes a double agent, working for both agencies, but most loyal to the principal with the highest Bond Strength.

entries.title: Short-Term Disguises
entries.summary: Rules for mundane disguises using the Guile Ability: an Intelligence + Guile roll made by the storyguide against a base Ease Factor, and an opposed Presence + Guile versus Intelligence + Folk Ken roll when interacting with someone.
quotes: To determine the success of a disguise, make an Intelligence + Guile roll, with a base Ease Factor of 9, modified according to the magnitude of the desired change, as laid out in the nearby insert.
Disguise Roll: Int + Guile + stress die vs. Ease Factor 9 + modifiers

entries.title: Deep Cover Disguises
entries.summary: Rules for long-term false identities: establishing a Reputation for the cover, how that Reputation reduces later Disguise rolls and grows with experience, the Virtue limits on roles, how it offsets the social penalty of The Gift, and how it fades when dormant.
quotes: This act grants a new Reputation as the disguised individual, at a score of 1 (see ArM5, page 167).
A character therefore subtracts his Reputation from the penalty to social rolls caused by The Gift, but only when dealing with those with whom he has regular contact.

entries.title: Disguise Roll Modifiers
entries.summary: A table of modifiers to the Disguise roll's Ease Factor for changes of social status, physical appearance or sex, and for how little preparation was possible.

entries.title: Hermetic Disguises and Personae
entries.summary: Notes on how the Code of Hermes treats magi who keep a disguise in another covenant or impersonate Quaesitores and Redcaps, including that magical impersonation can be prosecuted as scrying.
quotes: This magus was successfully prosecuted for scrying, because he used magic to take the appearance of the Redcap

entries.title: Personae (Persona Supernatural Virtue)
entries.summary: Explains how a magus with the Persona Virtue gains personae with a starting Reputation, how Persona experience carries over to their Reputations, what a persona cannot do, and how the magic is detected and counted as an equivalent spell level.
quotes: at the moment of transformation it can be detected as if it were a Muto Corpus spell of 10th level, but for every sunset or sunrise that passes after adopting the persona, the magnitude drops by one.
the equivalent spell level is equal to five times the score in the Ability

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.71

entries.title: Control Through Emotional Bonds
entries.summary: Introduces an optional network-of-influence system, adapted from other supplements, to model unexpected loyalties between noble allies whose tight emotional bonds make them act against their apparent interests. Troupes decide how far to use it.
quotes: The rules in this section are used to model the unexpected interactions between people whose tight emotional bonds make them do things which, superficially, are not in their own interests.

related.text: Merchant houses and magi's private agents (other supplements)

entries.title: Agents
entries.summary: Defines agents as directly controlled subordinates, gives the formula for how many a principal may have, and lists who does not count as an agent (magi, colorful characters, indirect subordinates, hirelings and other players' characters). A principal with weak Presence or Leadership can run a network through a single primary agent, called a factor.
quotes: 2 x (Presence + Intrigue or Leadership – social penalty for the Gift) or 1, whichever is larger.

entries.title: Design of Agents
entries.summary: The handful of statistics each agent needs: a name, a Social Status Virtue or Flaw, a Bond expressed as a Personality Trait, and the resources the principal can draw on through the agent. Worked examples show how a vassal and a bishop are built.
quotes: A Bond, which is a Personality Trait that expresses the reason for the agent's attachment to the principal, and its strength.

entries.title: Acquiring Agents
entries.summary: How characters gain agents, either at character creation through certain Virtues or in play by impressing a prospect with a Presence + Leadership roll and then wearing down his resistance with Agency Experience points. Includes the recruitment, task and persuasion tables.
quotes: Each of these virtues grants 12 points to spend on the accompanying Agent Recruitment Table for thematically appropriate agents.
a stress die + Presence + Leadership – social penalty for the Gift against an Ease Factor of 6.
A character's resistance is reduced by 1 in exchange for a number of Agency experience points equal to their current resistance.

entries.title: Agent Recruitment Table
entries.summary: Tables that set a potential agent's starting resistance from his Social Status, then adjust it for circumstances such as inconvenient Flaws and for the resources he can offer the principal.
quotes: A potential agent always has a minimum resistance score of 1.

entries.title: Tasks For Agents Table
entries.summary: Gives the persuasion Ease Factor for common agent tasks such as fetching information or performing easy, hard or impressive deeds, with modifiers for how quickly the task is needed and how much personal risk it carries.
quotes: Perform an Impressive Task (Ease Factor 18 or less).

entries.title: Agencies Overview
entries.summary: Introduces agencies, networks of mundane contacts through which a principal pursues goals without being implicated in meddling, and defines principals and agents.
quotes: A character controlling an agency is called its principal, in this chapter.
An agent is a person bound to offer assistance to a principal.

entries.title: Agents are Directly Controlled
entries.summary: Gives the formula for the maximum number of agents a principal can directly control, based on Presence, Intrigue or Leadership and the Gift's social penalty, and what happens if it is exceeded.
quotes: Maximum Number of Agents: [2 x (Presence + Intrigue
A character can always control one agent, no matter how poor his social skills or what the penalty of his Gift.

entries.title: Agents Act as Intermediaries (Factors)
entries.summary: Explains that most people commanded through an agency are resources controlled by an agent rather than extra agents, and introduces the factor, a single agent who runs the whole agency using his own statistics.
quotes: An agent employed to control an entire agency on behalf of a magus is called a factor.

entries.title: Designing Agents
entries.summary: Lists the few statistics needed for each agent (name, Social Status, Bond, resources) and the Difficult Underlings problem when a principal controls an agent of higher social standing, with magi exempt.
quotes: A Bond , which is a Personality Trait that expresses the reason that the agent is subordinate to the principal

entries.title: Partial Adoption (Agencies)
entries.summary: Optional approach in which troupes do not convert Virtues and Flaws such as Social Contacts or Close Family Ties into fully described agencies, tracking only agents gained during play.

entries.title: Recruiting Agents at Character Creation
entries.summary: Lists the Virtues and Flaws that grant an agency at the start of play and explains how to buy agents with agency points from the Resistance of Agents Table.
quotes: The player has 12 agency points to spend.

entries.title: Recruited Agents as Story Rewards
entries.summary: How to recruit an agent during play: impress the prospect with a roll, earn agency experience points from stories to wear down his Resistance Strength to zero, and build a Bond. Also covers inheriting an agency and why agents cannot be bought.
quotes: Impressing a Potential Agent: Presence + Leadership – social penalty of The Gift + stress die vs. Ease Factor 6
It takes the current value of a given Resistance Strength in agency experience points to decrease that strength by one

entries.title: Using Agents
entries.summary: How a principal sets agents tasks: a Persuasion Roll against an Ease Factor from the Tasks for Agents table, then a roll or side story for the task itself. Covers using agents for information or assistance and limits on how often they can be asked.
quotes: Persuasion Roll: Communication + Charm, Intrigue, or Leadership + Bond Strength – social penalty of The Gift + stress die vs. Ease Factor (see table under Tasks for Agents)

related.text: Modifiers to Persuasion Roll Ease Factors

versions.title: Using Agents
versions.summary: How a principal sets an agent a task with a persuasion roll against the Tasks for Agents table, how the agent then rolls his own Characteristics and Abilities, and how passive information gathering, active information gathering and requests for assistance are treated.
quotes: stress die + Communication + (Charm, Intrigue, or Leadership as situationally appropriate) + Bond Strength – social penalty of the Gift vs. an Ease factor on the Tasks for Agents table

entries.title: Resistance of Agents (rules)
entries.summary: Explains Resistance Strength, an agent's reluctance to serve, how it is reduced to zero and how the Bond Strength then grows, with a cap, and notes that Hermetic magi are never agents.
quotes: to a maximum of +6, representing a fanatically dedicated agent

entries.title: Confounding Situations
entries.summary: Guidance on how often an agent's Flaws make him unavailable to the principal, and how the Difficult Underlings Story Flaw applies to a whole agency.
quotes: an agent with a Minor Flaw might be unable to help his principal once out of every four requests

entries.title: Maintaining Agents
entries.summary: Agencies need upkeep: stories can lower an agent's Bond Strength, and it is raised through favors, which convert Adventure experience into agency experience, or money, which can only raise it up to a limit.
quotes: One Mythic Pound's worth of material goods can take the place of 5 agency experience points (or 4 shillings per point) without need for a story
Bond Strength can never rise above +3 by the application of money

versions.title: Maintaining Agents
versions.summary: How a principal keeps an agent's Bond from waning: by aiding the agent in stories and spending matching Agency experience points on the Bond, or less effectively by paying money.
quotes: A character may buy 5 Agency experience points per pound, and spend them as above to increase the bond of characters.

entries.title: Resistance of Agents Table
entries.summary: Tables of base Resistance by Social Status and the modifiers for Flaws, coercion and useful resources, used to cost agents at creation and to set the difficulty of recruiting them. A minimum applies.
quotes: A potential agent's Resistance cannot be less than 1.

entries.title: Tasks for Agents
entries.summary: Table of Ease Factors for the Persuasion Roll to get an agent to supply information or perform an easy, hard or impressive task.

entries.title: Modifiers to Persuasion Roll Ease Factors
entries.summary: Modifiers to a Persuasion Roll Ease Factor for how soon the task must be done and the personal risk to the agent, including the number of botch dice.

entries.title: Court Decisions (Quick Trial Roll)
entries.summary: A quick method to decide a trial: a social roll of Communication plus the relevant law Ability against an Ease Factor adjusted by the defendant's guilt, reputation and witnesses.
quotes: make a Communication + Civil and Canon Law roll against an Ease Factor of 6, on behalf of the defendant or his proxy
Defendant actually is innocent | –3

entries.title: Trial by Ordeal
entries.summary: Lists the types of judicial ordeal in Mythic Europe and notes a Just temper may arise around trials, favoring the innocent.
quotes: Their confidence could bring about a Just temper before the trial

versions.title: Trial by Ordeal
versions.requires: Defendant found guilty who insists on innocence
versions.summary: Summarises the four trials by ordeal (combat, cold water, hot water, iron) and what counts as proof of innocence in each.
quotes: A defendant who insists his innocence, even when the court finds him guilty, can choose to undergo a trial by ordeal.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.78

entries.title: Disputatio
entries.summary: Introduces the formal academic debate: its three types (epideictic, deliberative, forensic), the roles of opponent, responder and judge, and how questions and exchanges are structured.
quotes: Disputationes have a set number of questions, determined beforehand and usually numbering seven, nine, or twelve.

entries.title: Basic Disputatio
entries.summary: Resolves a disputatio like a certamen: each disputer's argument has symbolic Fatigue Levels worn down by Attack, Defense, Weakening and Resistance Totals, followed by an Over-Exertion check for real fatigue. Several Virtues and Flaws modify these totals.
quotes: Attack Total: Communication + Ability + stress die
Weakening Total: Intelligence + Attack Advantage
Disputatio Over-Exertion Check: Stamina + stress die vs. Ease Factor equal to the number of rounds of the disputatio

entries.title: Advanced Disputatio
entries.summary: Optional additions to the disputatio rules: minimum Ease Factors for statements, questions from the crowd, public Advent and Lent disputes, resolving a private examination as a disputatio, and experience rewards for winning.
quotes: Roll a stress die (no botch) to determine the Attack Total.
Disputatio experience point rewards should not be granted more than once a season.

entries.title: Schoolmen's Disputationes and House Tytalus' Debates
entries.summary: Explains how Tytalus debate differs from academic disputatio, how a Tytalus and an academic character debate each other, and when the Gift penalizes a disputatio.
quotes: Storyguides must determine if a –3 penalty is appropriate, depending on the situation.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates, House Tytalus

entries.title: The Fine Art of Debate
entries.summary: Introduces the debate rules, which have two parts: testing the strength of each side's position, then converting the result into the opinions of any observers.
quotes: The rules given below present a mechanic for settling an argument through debate.

entries.title: Resolving Differences (Debate Rounds)
entries.summary: The core debate procedure, modelled on certamen: each round the debaters pick an Attack Ability and Defense Ability and compare six totals, with debate fatigue, a table of attack modifiers by tactic and a worked example.
quotes: Attack Total: Communication + Attack Ability + attack modifier + stress die
Defense Total: Intelligence + Defense Ability + stress die
Weakening Total: Presence + Attack Advantage

entries.title: Winning Arguments
entries.summary: How to turn the result of a debate into votes from observers: divide them into factions, compute Argument Strength from Fatigue Levels lost, and read the share of neutral and hostile votes won from a table, with a worked example.
quotes: Argument Strength: Difference between the number of Fatigue Levels lost
If a debate ends because one opponent's argument loses 5 or more Fatigue Levels, then the winner is clear.

entries.title: The Power of Truth
entries.summary: Optional modifiers to debate: starting fatigued when defending a patently flawed thesis, and a penalty from the Truthful Personality Trait when knowingly arguing a falsehood.
quotes: If a character knows that the side he is taking is false, then his Defense Totals are penalized by his Truthful Personality Trait, if any.

entries.title: Using Certamen Instead of Debate
entries.summary: Says when certamen can replace a formal debate at Tribunal and how to work out Argument Strength when a certamen settles only one issue in a larger case.
quotes: In this situation, simply use the actual Fatigue Levels lost rather than debating Fatigue Levels when calculating the Argument Strength of the winner.

entries.title: Other Uses for the Debate Rules
entries.summary: Applies the voting system to mundane courts and English juries, including how jurors are assigned and how The Gift affects a magus's Defense Total.
quotes: If a character with The Gift is on trial, only 10% of the jurors begin the case sympathetic towards that character's position.
Furthermore, the social penalty of The Gift is applied to the Defense Total of a magus when debating with mundanes before witnesses.

entries.title: Case Rulings (Debate at Tribunal)
entries.summary: How a contested Tribunal case is debated, including the use of testimonies to boost Attack or Defense Totals once each, with a table of bonuses by type of testimony.
quotes: Each testimony possessed by an opponent may be used once per debate to support an argument.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, House Guernicus

entries.title: Proposal Cases (Debate at Tribunal)
entries.summary: How a magus proposing a clarification, addition or alteration to the Code is debated against the whole Tribunal, with a table of penalties to Argument Strength by type of case.
quotes: Once all the points have been debated, the proposer's Argument Strength is used to determine the margin of victory in the usual way.

entries.title: Magic for the Debating Arena
entries.summary: Covers using magic during Tribunal debates, how the Order frowns on it, and how self-enhancing spells can add bonuses to particular debate Defense Totals.
quotes: granting a +3 bonus to all debating Defense Totals that use the Leadership Ability

related.text: ArM5 p.145 Aura of Ennobled Presence

entries.title: Writing and Responding to Polemic
entries.summary: Introduces the activity of writing persuasive texts in advance of a Tribunal debate, using three forms of writing: polemic, diatribe and apologia.

entries.title: Polemic
entries.summary: A polemic is a summa or tractatus on a knowledge Ability such as Code of Hermes or Order of Hermes Lore that argues for a philosophical position; for these rules a polemic tractatus counts as Level 5.
quotes: tractatus have a Level of 5

entries.title: Diatribe
entries.summary: A diatribe is a critical text written on the same Ability as the polemic it attacks, intended to damage the position and its proponents; each tractatus counts against the author's normal tractatus limit.
quotes: Each tractatus counts towards the normal limit on the number of tractatus that the author may write.

entries.title: Apologia
entries.summary: An apologia is a defensive rebuttal written on the same Ability as the diatribe it answers, strengthening the original proposition; each tractatus counts against the author's normal limit.
quotes: Each tractatus counts towards the normal limit on the number of tractatus that the author may write.

entries.title: Like Father, Like Son (Views from Polemic)
entries.summary: A character who gains their first level in a knowledge Ability by reading a polemic is assumed to share the author's views on that subject.
quotes: any character gaining his first level in a knowledge Ability through reading polemic shares the author's views on that subject

entries.title: The Prevailing Wisdom
entries.summary: The base difficulty of altering opinion in writing depends on how broad the change is; the level is read from the Prevailing Wisdom table.

entries.title: Prevailing Wisdom Table
entries.summary: Table giving the base level of the prevailing wisdom according to whether the change concerns a magus, covenant, Tribunal, House or the whole Order.
quotes: The higher of 3 or the magus' reputation

entries.title: Prevailing Wisdom Examples
entries.summary: Table of sample topics with the Ease Factor that applies to changing opinion about them, and the reason for each.

entries.title: Winning the Argument
entries.summary: Describes how a polemic is written and why it must be of a level high enough to entice readers; its Quality contributes to a bonus in debate at Tribunal.
quotes: Polemical tractatus are treated as level 5 for the purposes of circulating them.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.91 Debate

entries.title: Circulating the Text
entries.summary: A polemic must be circulated through copies, with a seasonal Circulation Roll against an Ease Factor set by the audience; success grants the author a Supporter of (ideal) Reputation.
quotes: Circulation Total: Magus' Reputation + Summa Level (or 5 in the case of tractatus) + Simple Die
Ease Factor: 15 (Tribunal), 18 (House), 24 (the Order)
Each season spent circulating a text provides a bonus of +1 to the next Circulation Total.

entries.title: The Argument Total
entries.summary: Once circulated, the author works out an Argument Total from text quality minus the prevailing wisdom level, which converts into a debate bonus or penalty at Tribunal.
quotes: Argument Total: Text Quality – Prevailing Wisdom Level
the final Argument Total acts as experience points toward buying a debate bonus as per the Art progression table on

entries.title: Responding with Diatribe
entries.summary: A magus who studies a polemic for a season can write and circulate a diatribe whose quality is deducted from the Argument Total, gaining an Opposed to Reputation.
quotes: The diatribe quality is deducted from the current Argument Total

entries.title: Responding with Apologia
entries.summary: Apologia answer diatribes or the original polemic after a season of study and add their quality to the Argument Total; allies other than the original author can write them, and the writer gains a Supporter of Reputation.
quotes: the magus spends a season studying the associated work before writing either summa or tractatus in defense of the original argument

entries.title: Correspondences and Other Texts
entries.summary: Debate letters between quarreling magi give a small seasonal study benefit, can serve as supporting testimony in debate, and bundling extra new items with a polemic makes it easier to circulate.
quotes: gains +1 on attempts to circulate the text

entries.title: Winning the Argument Outline
entries.summary: Step-by-step summary of the polemic procedure from defining the argument and writing the text through circulation, apologia and diatribe to the final use of the Argument Total at Tribunal.
quotes: At Tribunal the argument total is used as experience points to buy a bonus (if the total is positive) or a penalty (if the total is negative).

entries.title: Example Polemic, Diatribe, and Apologia
entries.summary: Worked example of writing, circulating and opposing a polemic, showing Quality, circulation totals and the resulting Argument Total and debate bonus.
quotes: The polemic has a Level of 4 and a Quality of 11

groups.title: Courtly life and leisure
groups.intro: Hospitality, feasts, romance, patronage, hunting and hawking.

entries.title: Board Games
entries.summary: Describes period board games and the social value of playing them well, noting that Carouse may win a game but Etiquette is also needed to impress an opponent.
quotes: Playing well is a social grace, and while the Carouse Ability may allow a win, Etiquette is needed as well to impress one's opponent in what is, after all, a pursuit of polite company.

entries.title: Gambling
entries.summary: Notes common dice games and that Legerdemain or Luck can alter a die, and says which Abilities underlie gambling: Carouse for games of chance and Concentration for games of skill.
quotes: Games of chance are based upon the Ability Carouse, games of skill upon the Ability Concentration.

related.text: Tales of Mythic Europe: The Ship of Desire

entries.title: A Game of Chance?
entries.summary: Explains that imperfect dice let a skilled player gain an advantage with Perception + Carouse, with Luck and Legerdemain giving further edges and cheating leading to brawls.
quotes: use Perception + Carouse Ability to gain an advantage over an unskilled player

entries.title: Good Drink, Song, and Dance
entries.summary: Entertainment in noble halls and the dances of the period; knowing court dance steps uses Etiquette, local folk dances use Area Lore, and performing well depends on Athletics.
quotes: While knowledge of the steps of any given court dance is based upon Etiquette (local folk dances fall under Area Lore), a successful performance depends upon the Ability Athletics.

entries.title: The Feast
entries.summary: Introduces the noble feast as a frequent and special event, and notes that a host who fails to put on a feast for a guest earns a Reputation for being inhospitable.
quotes: a host who does not put on a feast for a guest will soon gain a Reputation for being inhospitable

entries.title: Seating the Guests, and Good Manners
entries.summary: How a hall is laid out and guests are seated by precedence, with Etiquette used to place guests correctly, and the contrast between Etiquette at the high table and Carouse at the lower tables.
quotes: Placing someone in too low a position can be seen as an insult, so Etiquette is used to decide the correct seating.

entries.title: The Host
entries.summary: How the quality of hospitality affects a host, including the insult of poor hospitality, the use by kings of demanded hospitality to weaken vassals, and the Reputation (or even a Gratitude point) earned by an exceptional feast.
quotes: a good host who puts on a lavish feast will soon gain a Reputation for hospitality and generosity, and for feasts that are exceptional in food, entertainment, and gifts, even a Gratitude point

entries.title: The Hunt
entries.summary: Why nobles hunt, hunting rights in chases, warrens and forests, poaching, and the etiquette of noble hunting, including that spells making prey fall dead breach etiquette and that hunting sick prey costs Reputation.
quotes: A chase or warren is a Minor Surroundings Boon
Spells that cause the prey to simply fall over dead, or otherwise fail to provide a challenging pursuit, are, however, regarded as a breach of etiquette

entries.title: Varieties of Hunting Hounds
entries.summary: The classes of hunting dog (lymers, running dogs, greyhounds, alaunts, mastiffs, harriers and bird dogs), what each does in a hunt, and the master of kennels who trains them.
quotes: The main classes are lymers, running dogs, greyhounds, alaunts, mastiffs, harriers, and bird dogs.

entries.title: Hounds and Aging
entries.summary: Optional aging rules for important hounds: when they begin to age, how often they roll, how the modifier grows, and how kennels with a Master of Kennels give a Living Conditions bonus.
quotes: A dog begins to age at ten years, and must make an Aging roll every season thereafter except in the spring, rather than every year as with a human.

entries.title: Hunting with Hounds
entries.summary: Introduces the most prestigious form of hunting, whose general format anyone with the Etiquette Ability knows, and which the following stage-by-stage sections detail.
quotes: the general format is known and accepted by anyone with a score in the Ability Etiquette

entries.title: The Quest
entries.summary: First stage of a formal hunt: huntsmen with lymers track and assess prey using a tracking roll, a roll to keep the lymer quiet, and a roll to judge the quarry's age and condition.
quotes: Huntsmen each make Perception + (the lymer's or huntsman's Hunt Ability, whichever is lower) rolls against Ease Factor 9, to track an appropriate beast to its lair.

entries.title: The Assembly
entries.summary: The breakfast at which huntsmen present their finds and guests inspect droppings with a Perception + Hunt test to choose the day's prey.
quotes: These are examined with a test of Perception +Hunt against Ease Factor 12

entries.title: The Relay
entries.summary: Positioning of the running dogs, greyhounds, alaunts and mastiffs in advance along the prey's likely path, using Area Lore and Hunting, and what happens if the dogs are poorly placed.
quotes: Area Lore is essential to understand the lay of the land, and the Ability Hunting to predict the pursued animal's erratic path correctly.

entries.title: The Chase
entries.summary: The core hunt resolution: each hourly round hunters roll to keep up, hounds and prey lose fatigue unless they pass Stamina rolls, and the hounds' Pursuit Total is compared to the prey's Evasion Total to decide who wins each round until one side has won enough rounds.
quotes: Each round of the chase represents one hour of pursuit, and requires a Dexterity + Ride stress roll against Ease Factor 6 to keep in sight of the hounds.
Pursuit Total: Hound's Perception + hound's Hunt + stress die – lowest Fatigue penalty among the hounds vs.
Evasion Total: Prey's Dexterity + Athletics + Terrain Bonus (starts at 6) + stress die – Fatigue penalty

entries.title: The Kill
entries.summary: After the prey is cornered the hunters dismount to kill it, best resolved as a melee combat against an already fatigued quarry.
quotes: This is best resolved as a melee combat, but as the prey is typically fatigued it is normally over swiftly.

entries.title: The Unmaking and Curee
entries.summary: The formal butchering of the quarry and rewarding of the dogs, with its customs represented by the Hunt Ability, and the note that informal hunts are also common.
quotes: There is a formal set of customs to this, represented by the Hunt Ability

entries.title: Bow and Stable Hunting
entries.summary: A drive hunt with archers and mounted beaters, which takes much game but has lower status than hunting with hounds except in certain Tribunals.
quotes: bow and stable hunting lacks the status of hunting with hounds

entries.title: The Terrain Bonus
entries.summary: A bonus added to the prey's Evasion Total when it is native to the terrain, and the per-round rolls by the relay planners and hunters that can reduce it, even turning it into a penalty over a long hunt.
quotes: This is reflected in a Terrain Bonus of +6 added to the prey's Evasion Total.
Every round, any character who participated in establishing the relay must make a stress roll of Intelligence + Hunt + 6 against an Ease Factor equal to the Evasion Total.

entries.title: The Prey
entries.summary: Which animals nobles hunt and when: the preference order from magical animals through Beasts of Virtue to the finest mundane game, the seasons of the hart, boar and bear, and the prestige (or lack of it) of hunting hare, wolf, fox and otter.
quotes: The order of preference for prey begins with powerful, unusual, and exotic magical animals (especially those that offer a great challenge and threaten the estate); continues to Beasts of Virtue; and ends with the very best specimens of mundane animals.

related.text: The Book of Mundane Beasts, Realms of Power: Magic pp.140-144

entries.title: Horses
entries.summary: Explains that medieval horses are classed by role rather than breed, the status and cost issues of owning horses, and the roles of mares and stallions in farming, travel and war.
quotes: Medieval horses are not differentiated from one another by breed, but rather by their suitability for certain roles.

entries.title: Horses and Aging
entries.summary: Optional aging rules for important horses: lifespan, when a horse begins to age, rolling every season, and the stable bonus that needs a Profession Marshal score; also a loss of horses in a shoddy stable and the carrying capacity rule of thumb in the following sidebar.
quotes: A horse begins to age at 14 years, and must make an aging roll every season thereafter, rather than every year as humans do.
Every five years a horse's aging modifier increases by one.

entries.title: A Note on Size and Capacity
entries.summary: Explains how horses are measured in hands and gives a rule of thumb for how much weight a horse can carry unencumbered.
quotes: A horse can carry unencumbered about 30% of its weight in pounds

entries.title: Hawking
entries.summary: How noble hawking works: the hawker rolls to release and command the bird, and a results table says how aggressively the hawk attacks its prey.
quotes: The mechanics of hunting require a Presence + Animal Handling roll from the hawker, as he releases the hawk and issues commands.

entries.title: Birds and Aging
entries.summary: Optional rules for aging individual birds of prey, which age on a faster schedule than humans.
quotes: A hawk or falcon begins to age at ten years, and must make an Aging roll every season thereafter
Every four years after age ten the aging modifier increases by 1.

entries.title: Running an Establishment
entries.summary: General system for the quality, capacity, upkeep and staffing of kennels, mews and stables, including what happens when maintenance is not paid; includes a modifiable gyrfalcon template for other hawks and falcons.
quotes: Reduce the number of animals by 15% (round up) for each season these requirements are not met.
Failure to meet the annual maintenance cost results in the establishment dropping to the next lower level of quality immediately.

entries.title: The Kennels
entries.summary: What a kennel contains, giving the standard mix of hound types and how larger qualities scale it up.
quotes: for every 12 running dogs there is one lymer and three greyhounds or alaunts

entries.title: Kennels, Mews, and Stables Tables
entries.summary: Tables giving capacity, yearly maintenance cost, staff and Living Conditions modifier for each quality of kennel, mews and stables.

entries.title: Living Conditions and Specialists
entries.summary: The specialist Ability needed to benefit from an establishment's positive Living Conditions modifier, and the yearly winter roll that decides whether it is well run or declines.
quotes: A stress roll of Intelligence + Animal Handling against Ease Factor 9
a score in the relevant Profession Ability equal to at least twice the Living Conditions modifier

entries.title: Is Love True?
entries.summary: Guidance for the troupe on whether and how courtly love features in the saga, with three rules of thumb for romance subplots.
quotes: no character with the True Love or Lost Love Virtue or Flaw may ever be caught up in romance, except with the object of their affections.

entries.title: Patronage
entries.summary: How giving gifts, grants and support to a specific social group earns a Reputation with that group, a Loyal Trait in the recipient and sometimes Gratitude, with notes on each kind of patron-recipient group.
quotes: improves a Loyal Personality Trait in the recipient that is directed toward the patron
Reputations can pertain to Local (meaning all in the vicinity), Clergy, Order of Hermes, Nobles, or Academics.

entries.title: Etiquette Performances
entries.summary: Introduces etiquette as symbolic communication at events and the three kinds of performance a character can attempt; an observer can tell which kind is being attempted with a roll.
quotes: an Intelligence + Etiquette roll against an Ease Factor of 3

entries.title: Individual Etiquette
entries.summary: Communication + Etiquette roll against a host-set Ease Factor to be the most memorable attendee at an event and earn Reputation experience; results can be given to another person.
quotes: A character wishing to make an individual impression at an event makes a Communication + Etiquette roll.
At minimum this is 6, but can be as high as 21.

entries.title: Competitive Etiquette (Etiquette Duels)
entries.summary: Etiquette duel in which each rival chooses a self-inflicted penalty to impose on both Communication + Etiquette rolls, then results are compared to see who looks boorish or wins the exchange.
quotes: A participant cannot choose a penalty greater than his Etiquette score.
The sum of both selected penalties is subtracted from the standard Etiquette roll of both individuals.

entries.title: Collaborative Etiquette
entries.summary: Group etiquette where participants' rolls are summed into a score compared with past events, with penalties for botches and sample scores for Tribunal feasts, Primus elections and symposia.
quotes: the rolls of all participants are added together
A person who botches during such an event reduces the score by 10, and may develop a poor Reputation.

entries.title: Money and Good Manners
entries.summary: Rules for boosting an Etiquette roll by spending money or by giving suitable gifts, and a roll to learn what gifts a particular magus would value.
quotes: The bonus is equal to +1 for each time the character spends the weekly income of all of his guests.
A character cannot gain a bonus higher than his Etiquette score by spending money.
An Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore + Reputation (of the receiver) roll against an Ease Factor of

entries.title: Hermetic Courtesy and Hospitality
entries.summary: Jerbiton code of conduct listing the obligations of guests and hosts when visiting another Jerbiton magus's territory; breaking it is taken as a deliberate insult.
quotes: It is rude to refuse to offer hospitality, but it is also rude to demand it.

groups.title: Family and women
groups.intro: Marriage, inheritance and the public power of women.

entries.title: Public Power for Women
entries.summary: Introduces how women gain public power in Mythic Europe, framed as material for storytelling rather than prohibition, and points to the Paid Rights Virtue for exceptional women characters.
quotes: The Paid Rights Virtue (page 100) is a gamemechanical way to acknowledge that an exceptional woman is just that: exceptional.

entries.title: Dressing As A Man
entries.summary: The simplest way for a woman to avoid social conventions: dressing as a man, which may become a Dark Secret and may qualify for Gender Nonconforming.
quotes: This may become a Dark Secret (page 124), and may also qualify the character for Gender Nonconforming (page 131).

entries.title: Holding Land (Women)
entries.summary: The six ways a woman can come to control land (absence, inheritance, political success, conquest, widow's portion, stewardship) with notes on how each works in practice and a rule of thumb for a widow's income.
quotes: Women can gain control of land in six ways: during absence, through inheritance, via political success, through conquest, in a widow's portion, or as a steward.
As a rule of thumb, assume a widow can keep the profit, not income, of a third of her husband's land until she remarries.

versions.title: Holding Land
versions.summary: Lists the six ways a woman can gain control of land, each of which is then detailed in a subsection.
quotes: Women can gain control of land in six ways: during absence, through inheritance, via political success, through conquest, in a widow's portion, or as a steward.

entries.title: Designing a Family
entries.summary: How a player may pick or randomly generate siblings and bastards for a noble character, set their birth order, and roll each sibling's Loyal Personality Trait toward the head of the family. Explains how primogeniture and military inclination change those loyalty results.
quotes: roll two dice of different colors and halve each result
The maximum score is 3 and negative scores are permitted.

entries.title: Inheritance
entries.summary: Describes how land passes to sons, nominated heirs, appanages or daughters in different parts of Mythic Europe, and the measures nobles use to limit fratricide.
quotes: The average noble family fails to provide a male heir every fourth generation, so this churning of lands is common.

entries.title: Marriage and Dowries
entries.summary: How noble marriages are arranged, what the Church requires, and how dowries and widows' portions are handled in Italy, France and England, with a game-ready rule of thumb for a widow's share.
quotes: For game purposes, assume this is one third of his estate, and that she likely loses this property if she remarries.

versions.title: Marriage and Dowries
versions.summary: How marriage consent and dowries work for merchants, including a husband's rights over a dowry in Italy, France and England and the share of an estate a widow keeps for game purposes.
quotes: For game purposes, assume this is one third of his estate, and that she likely loses this property if she remarries.

entries.title: Size of Dowries
entries.summary: A checklist of circumstances that push a bride's dowry down, with the note that dowries are more generous when those statements are untrue and that an exceptional bride may even earn her family a dower.
quotes: Conversely, dowries are more generous if any of these statements are untrue.

entries.title: Absence
entries.summary: How a noblewoman acts as deputy while her husband is away: her Abilities, her right to spend the income and command vassals, her role in siege defense and her networks of agents.
quotes: Women raised for this task always have Leadership and Profession: Steward scores.

entries.title: Inheritance
entries.summary: How women inherit land in different parts of Europe, whether they keep legal authority in marriage, and how dowry land relates to inheritance.
quotes: A woman who rules a fief by inheritance usually retains legal authority in it during her marriage.

entries.title: Widow's Portion and Stewardship
entries.summary: A rule of thumb for how much of her late husband's land a widow can keep and when she regains full ownership of her own lands.
quotes: As a rule of thumb, assume a widow can keep the profit, not income, of a third of her husband's land until she remarries.

entries.title: A Note on Life Expectancy
entries.summary: Advises storyguides who want female nobles to hold power to cull male NPCs using the random method of death given earlier.
quotes: Players in sagas designed for female nobles to play a significant role need to consciously cull male non-player characters.

entries.title: Women as Warriors
entries.summary: Notes how cultures react to women acting as knights and the Hermetic attitude toward it, with five historical examples (dressing as a man, inheritance, conquest, absence and political success) to guide backgrounds for female nobles seeking military roles.
quotes: The following examples may guide the generation of background for female nobles who seek military roles.

entries.title: Nuns
entries.summary: The Church as a third avenue of power for women: nuns' legal status, their land, temporary vows and the use of nunneries as refuge.
quotes: Nuns are considered wards of the bishop, and brides of Christ.

entries.title: Family and Inheritance
entries.summary: How a magus's birth or adoptive family interacts with the Gift and with law: choosing apprentices, and why magi cannot hold feudal land but may inherit other property and have stewards for child heirs.
quotes: Magi may not enter into feudal relationships, and so may not inherit land.

entries.title: Nepotism
entries.summary: Optional use of family members as agents: the player links story events to their fortunes so Bond Maintenance points from adventure experience can be spent on them.
quotes: This allows the magus to spend Bond Maintenance points, which equal the Adventure experience they receive for the story, on their family members.

entries.title: Family Reputation
entries.summary: Families carry shared Reputations that characters may use instead of their own among strangers, shaped by every family member's actions.
quotes: characters may use this Reputation instead of their own, among people who do not personally know the character

entries.title: Calculating Dowries for Merchants' Daughters
entries.summary: Sidebar procedure for working out a bride's dowry from her father's annual profit and Social Status relative to the groom, with factors that make a dowry larger or smaller.
quotes: This is figured by multiplying the father's annual profit by 10, then dividing by the number of children he has, except any daughters already married.

entries.title: Paid Rights: A Free Virtue
entries.requires: Female character who has paid a fine for a normally forbidden right
entries.summary: Lets a woman character who paid a large fine or fee before play to hold a right normally forbidden to women take a free Virtue called Paid Rights, optionally balanced by a Story Flaw. It cannot buy anything that only men may do in Church administration, and knighthood is difficult.
quotes: She may choose a free Virtue, called Paid Rights, to note that she has paid for the right to do a certain thing that is generally forbidden for women.

groups.title: Artists and art
groups.intro: Artists, their works, Reputation and sponsors.

entries.title: Artists and Artwork (Craft vs. Profession)
entries.summary: Explains how the book splits artists into production artists (who use a Craft Ability) and performance artists (who use a Profession Ability), which free Social Status Virtue each should take, and what counts as artwork (with an Aesthetic Quality) rather than a manufactured item.
quotes: Production artists should take the free Social Status Virtue: Craftsman, and performance artists should take the free Social Status Virtue: Wanderer.
Every piece of artwork has an Aesthetic Quality that determines how beautiful it is.

entries.title: Identifying an Artist's Work
entries.summary: Describes how production artists work for a select clientele and gives the rolls for recognising who made a piece of artwork, with artists identifying work more easily than non-artists and a higher Reputation making it easier still.
quotes: An artist character can identify an artwork's creator with a Perception + the creator's (Artist) Reputation + a simple die roll against an Ease Factor of 15.
Non-artist characters may identify a particular piece of artwork with a Perception + the creator's (Artist) Reputation + simple die roll against an Ease Factor of 18.

entries.title: Vernacular Literature: Writing and Studying Poetry
entries.summary: Vernacular literature has an Aesthetic Quality rather than a Source Quality, and a poet may write it in any language he knows well enough and whose alphabet he can write. Poets can study other poets' work to raise Craft: Poetry, and non-poets can spend a season reading it for exposure experience in Abilities the storyguide picks.
quotes: The poet can write it in any language in which he has a score of 5
The character gains exposure experience points that can apply to any of the various topics the piece might cover.

entries.title: Performers' (Profession) Ability and Picking Pockets
entries.summary: Explains when a performer uses his (Profession) Ability and when a general Ability applies, and when the Profession may substitute for a physical Ability such as Athletics or Brawl. Also gives the roll for performers who captivate a crowd while a thief among them picks pockets.
quotes: Dexterity + (Profession) Ability + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12
the thief gets a +3 bonus to his roll

entries.title: Styles of Music
entries.summary: Each musician character has a base regional style of music, and studying a different style for a season grants a one-time bonus of experience points that grows with the distance of the new style from the character's own.
quotes: he receives a one-time study bonus of 1 to 3 extra experience points

entries.title: Minstrels Who Are Also Poets
entries.summary: A minstrel who is also a poet holds both a Profession Ability and a Craft Ability, using the Profession to set the Aesthetic Quality of a song and the Craft: Poetry to set the Aesthetic Quality of a written poem.
quotes: When composing a song, he would use his Profession: Minnesinger Ability to determine the song's Aesthetic Quality.

entries.title: Creating Art: Fame, Muses and Artist Reputation Goal
entries.summary: Introduces the artist's career arc in game terms: a successful artist attracts a muse, a supernatural patron who eventually carries him to a realm of immortality, and his (Artist) Reputation grows from the quality of his work, his benefactor's power and the praise he receives.
quotes: In game terms, every artist character strives to reach an (Artist) Reputation of 10, achieving various benefits along the way.

entries.title: Aesthetic Quality of Artwork
entries.summary: Every piece of artwork has an Aesthetic Quality, worked out from Dexterity plus a Craft Ability for production arts or Communication plus a Profession Ability for performance arts, then modified by listed bonuses such as Virtues, extra time, overtime, liberal arts knowledge, a muse and, for legendary artists, the local aura. A player may also gamble on experimentation, rolling a bonus die and then consulting the experimentation results.
quotes: Aesthetic Quality: Dexterity + Craft Ability + bonuses OR Communication + Profession Ability + bonuses
An artist can double the time it takes to create a piece of artwork and receive a +1 bonus.

entries.title: Time Spent Creating Artwork
entries.summary: Gives base creation times for different kinds of artwork (a season, a year or decades), scales that time by the piece's Aesthetic Quality, and explains how assistants limited by Leadership and deliberately hurried work change the time taken. Artists also use the usual free and work seasons, with work seasons earning exposure experience.
quotes: multiply it by 1/10 the Aesthetic Quality of the expected finished piece to determine the full length of time required
The creating character can have assistants equal to his Leadership score.
Doing this divides a piece's Aesthetic Quality by half.

related.text: ArM5 p.163 free and work seasons

entries.title: Artist Experimentation Results
entries.summary: A table and explanation of what happens when an artist experiments with a piece: results run from disaster and ruined artwork through no effect to the artwork or the artist being praised, affecting Aesthetic Quality and (Artist) Reputation.
quotes: The character gains experience points in his (Artist) Reputation equal to the Aesthetic Quality of the piece.
The art is so excellent that the artist gains enough experience points to raise his (Artist) Reputation score one whole level.

entries.title: Performing a Performance
entries.summary: A performer fixes the Aesthetic Quality of a routine, play or song when first creating it, and normally no further roll is needed. In unusual circumstances the storyguide calls for a roll, using the highest-skilled participant for group performances.
quotes: Communication or Dexterity + Profession Ability + stress die vs. Aesthetic Quality/2

entries.title: Art as an Arcane Connection
entries.summary: An original piece of artwork acts as an Arcane Connection to its creator for a limited time that depends on how long it took to make, shortened by assistants, while copies and very large works do not count. Performances need Imaginem magic to capture, and the connection can be fixed like any other.
quotes: a piece of art maintains an Arcane Connection to its creator for a length of time equal to half the time it took to create it
Subtract one week from the length of time an Arcane Connection lasts for every assistant the creating artist had.

entries.title: Studying Artwork as an Advancement Source
entries.summary: Artists can study another artist's piece in the same Craft or Profession as a season of study, using half its Aesthetic Quality as the Advancement total. Performances must be practised and contemplated, each work can be studied only once, and a character cannot study his own work.
quotes: Divide the artwork's Aesthetic Quality by two to determine the Advancement total.
Source Quality: Aesthetic Quality/2

entries.title: Gaining and Losing Artist Reputation
entries.summary: An artist character keeps a separate (Artist) Reputation for each Craft or Profession, which grows like an Ability from experience points earned specifically for it. The usual source is completing artwork of high enough Aesthetic Quality, with further lists of events that add or subtract Reputation experience points.
quotes: Aesthetic Quality greater than 3 times Artist Reputation = 1 Artist Reputation experience point
Gaining a patron grants 6 experience points
Losing a patron subtracts 12 experience points

entries.title: Benefits of Artist Reputation
entries.summary: Describes what each Artist Reputation threshold gives: a bonus to impressive social rolls, a minor muse, the right to sign work and a Confidence increase, a major muse, a permanent bonus to Aesthetic Quality, and finally legendary status. It also covers losing Reputation through truly deplorable behavior.
quotes: Once a character's Artist Reputation is 6, she can add +1 to any social roll in which her status would impress or influence a person.
the character does receive a 1-point increase in his Confidence Score when his Artist Reputation reaches 8
He gains a permanent +3 to the final Aesthetic Quality of his artwork, added on top of the normal calculation.

entries.title: Legendary Artists
entries.summary: Explains what happens to an artist who becomes a legendary artist: he becomes an immortal creature of his muse's realm with a Might score and powers based on his art, is vulnerable to Hermetic magic affecting supernatural beings, and can keep gained experience only by means of mnemonic artwork or a supernatural familiar.
quotes: He gains a Might score equal to two times his highest Craft or Profession Ability, and a number of supernatural powers equal to that same Craft or Profession Ability.
The piece of artwork must have a finished Aesthetic Quality equal to twice the number of recently gained experience points.
Each point of Might allows the artist to retain 5 experience points from study.

entries.title: Muses
entries.summary: Describes muses as supernatural patrons of any realm, divided into minor and major by Might. A muse can temporarily sacrifice some of its Might to grant the artist supernatural Virtues or powers, and the bond brings Warping to the artist.
quotes: A minor muse is any supernatural creature that acts as an artist's patron and has a Might score of 15 or less.
Minor muses may sacrifice 5 points of Might and grant the character a minor, supernatural Virtue.
The artist gains 1 Warping point a year from a minor muse and 3 from a major muse.

entries.title: Sponsors: Patrons and Benefactors
entries.summary: Every artwork needs a sponsor, either a benefactor for one piece or a patron for ongoing support. The artist spends a season rolling to find one, with modifiers by sponsor type and standing, increasingly wealthy sponsors required as Reputation grows, a ways to lose a sponsor, and a minimum payment when a player character sponsors an artist.
quotes: Finding a Sponsor: Communication + Bargain + Artist Reputation + stress die vs. 12 + modifiers
A player can make a Perception + Folk Ken + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12.
Cost to Sponsor an Artwork (Completed in One Season): At least 1 Mythic Pound per point of Artist Reputation

entries.title: Magically Created Art
entries.summary: Magi can create artwork instantly using the mundane-object creation rules, rolling Finesse to determine the Aesthetic Quality. Mundane artists cannot gain experience by studying such art, and intangible art needs Mentem magic.
quotes: Magically Created Art Aesthetic Quality: Intelligence + Finesse, –6, –9, –12, or –15

entries.title: Instilling Magic Effects in Artwork
entries.requires: Maestro with Virtue: Hermetic Inclination in (Form)
entries.summary: Hermetic magi instill effects into artwork by the normal procedure, ignoring Aesthetic Quality. Maestros with Hermetic Inclination instead build the effect while making the piece, accumulating points from an Ability total against the effect level and paying Fatigue for higher-level effects.
quotes: the player compares his character's Dexterity + Craft Ability + Form to the final level of the effect
Instilling a magical effect in a piece of artwork costs a Fatigue Level per 10 levels of the spell-like power.

related.text: ArM5 p.97 Material and Size Table
